The cardinality of a finite set $A$ is the number of elements in $A.$ 

Notice that the elements of our set 

$$
-875,\,-869,\,-863,\,…
$$

form an arithmetic sequence with a common difference $d=6:$

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =6 \\  & =-869-(-875) \\  & =-863-(-869) \\  & =⋯\end{aligned}
$$

The $n$th term of our arithmetic sequence, denoted ${a}_{n},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & =-875+(n-1)\cdot 6 \\  & =-875+6n-6 \\  & =6n-881.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can express $A$ in set-builder notation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={6n-881:n\in N,\,1\le n\le N}\end{aligned}
$$

where $N\in N$ is to be determined.

To find $N,$ we solve the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}6N-881 & =6\,151 \\ 6N & =7\,032 \\ N & =\frac{7\,032}{6} \\ N & =1\,172\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our set $A$ can be expressed as

$$
A={6n-881:n\in N,\,1\le n\le 1\,172}.
$$

Finally, since $A$ has $1\,172$ elements, we must have $|A|=1\,172.$
